passage.title: Accountability and Responsible Leadership
paras: Accountability means that people with power must explain and answer for what they do. Without it, power is easily misused.

Democracies build in several checks. Elections let citizens remove leaders who fail them. Independent courts can rule that a government has broken the law. A free press can investigate and report wrongdoing. In the UK, Parliament questions ministers, and every week the Prime Minister must answer MPs' questions in public.
Transparency, being open about decisions and spending, makes accountability possible. If people cannot see what leaders are doing, they cannot challenge it.

Corruption grows where these checks are weak: where leaders control the courts, silence journalists and hide accounts. In Animal Farm, the pigs do all three, and the other animals are left unable even to remember what the rules once said.
Accountability is not an insult to good leaders. It protects them from temptation and protects everyone else from harm.
